title: Treasury non-inversion full-capital BTC long/cash timing
thesis: A non-inverted U.S. Treasury term spread may identify macroeconomic and risk-bearing conditions in which holding unlevered spot BTC is better compensated, while a negative spread may precede adverse risk paths. Holding BTC only when the latest published 10-year minus 3-month spread is non-negative may improve drawdown and Calmar without forfeiting too much after-cost upside.
mechanism: Use the latest official Treasury trading-day 10-year and 3-month constant-maturity par yields only after 00:00 UTC on the next calendar day. Hold 100-percent BTC when 10Y minus 3M is at or above zero and zero-yield cash otherwise. Execute changed targets at the next H1 open. Test 10Y minus 1Y and 10Y minus 2Y only as frozen rejection neighbors.
economic_rationale: The rule is useful only if avoiding inversion-associated macro risk reduces matched-capital drawdown and underwater paths enough to offset missed BTC rallies, cash opportunity cost and round-trip friction. Positive aggregate PnL is insufficient; Design, Validation, annual breadth, realized/unrealized accounting, holding, terminal inventory and both common-maturity neighbors must support the mechanism.
